name: Main Salmon — Corn Creek to Carey Creek
description: The Main Salmon River run from Corn Creek to Vinegar Creek covers approximately 79 miles through the Salmon River Canyon in central Idaho, one of the deepest river gorges in North America. The canyon passes through a mix of wilderness and ranch land, with evidence of the region's mining and homesteading history visible at several points along the route. The run typically takes four to six days to complete. Like the Middle Fork, private launches during peak season require a permit obtained through a lottery system, and the remote nature of the put-in at Corn Creek makes shuttle logistics a significant part of trip planning.
hazards: Permit required for private launches during peak season (Four Rivers Lottery, recreation.gov)
Deep canyon with limited road access — long shuttle Corn Creek → Carey Creek
Big-water Class III–IV rapids at high flows
points_of_interest: Devil's Teeth Rapid — big waves at high water
Salmon Falls Rapid — one of the sportiest drops on the run
Bailey Creek and Chittam Rapids — big-water finales in Carey Falls Canyon
Multiple hot springs and historic homesteads along the canyon
usgs_site_name: Salmon River near Shoup (13307000) + Middle Fork Salmon at Mouth (13310199), combined
